sn35.30:1.1: “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the way that is appropriate for uprooting all conceivings.
sn35.30:1.2: Listen to that and attend closely, I will speak….
sn35.30:1.3: “And what, bhikkhus, is the way that is appropriate for uprooting all conceivings?
sn35.30:1.4: Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu does not conceive the eye, does not conceive in the eye, does not conceive from the eye, does not conceive, ‘The eye is mine.’
sn35.30:1.8: and as to whatever feeling arises with eye-contact as condition—whether pleasant or painful or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—he does not conceive that, does not conceive in that, does not conceive from that, does not conceive, ‘That is mine.’
sn35.30:1.14: He does not conceive the mind …
sn35.30:1.18: mind-consciousness … mind-contact … and as to whatever feeling arises with mind-contact as condition … he does not conceive that, does not conceive in that, does not conceive from that, does not conceive, ‘That is mine.’
sn35.30:1.19: “He does not conceive all, does not conceive in all, does not conceive from all, does not conceive, ‘All is mine.’
sn35.30:1.20: “Since he does not conceive anything thus, he does not cling to anything in the world.
sn35.30:1.21: Not clinging, he is not agitated. Being unagitated, he personally attains Nibbāna.
sn35.30:1.22: He understands: ‘Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’
sn35.30:1.23: “This, bhikkhus, is the way that is appropriate for uprooting all conceivings.”
